A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe MAIN. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F in v2 and A–H in v3 are readable and support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning benchmark results, filtering and iteration ablations, and GPT-4 pairwise evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds multilingual evaluations and an MMLU filtering analysis in Appendices D and F.

M1.justification: Section 2, Algorithm 1, and equations 1–8 retain the same alternating forward/reverse optimization, dynamic weighting, augmentation, and mutual filtering. The added experiments apply the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix D substantially extends the English-focused coverage to French, Japanese, Spanish, Arabic, and Chinese. It adds multilingual OpenAssistant and mC4 training data, mIFEval evaluations in three languages, and Japanese, Arabic, and Chinese MMLU benchmarks.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain Humpback, Longform, Dog Instruct, and Better Alignment. The new multilingual comparison reuses Humpback and Better Alignment, while the new MMLU analysis reuses existing no-filter and mutual-filter variants. No retained comparison changes comparator membership.

E3.justification: v3 adds protocols for the new experiments: balanced multilingual sampling of 3.2k seed pairs, 500k mC4 responses, 20k final training pairs, and five-shot multilingual reasoning evaluation. Appendix F adds controlled filtering comparisons by MMLU super-category. Previously reported protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a targeted analysis of whether filtering helps different MMLU categories, comparing aligned models with and without filtering while holding other settings fixed. Existing filtering, iteration-count, dynamic-weighting, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing results are unchanged, but Tables 8 and 10 substantially expand the findings. MAIN leads five of six multilingual evaluations; French mIFEval is 69.7 versus Better Alignment's 65.3, while AMMLU is 59.6 versus 59.8. The new MMLU ablation reports 44.1% without filtering and 45.4% with filtering, including a 2.8-point STEM gain.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, optimization equations, and formal method description are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear in the added appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about mutual alignment, filtering, and effectiveness across model families and scales. Additional multilingual evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new evaluations as supporting multilingual applicability. Appendix F additionally attributes larger STEM gains to tighter, more deterministic instruction-response relationships and explains smaller gains in open-ended categories. The limitation concerning very large models is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, documents multilingual sampling and training quantities, and supplies response/instruction placeholders in the GPT-4 evaluation template. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and computational-cost estimates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. MAIN retains the same positioning relative to instruction back-translation and other instruction-data generation approaches.

P1.justification: v3 adds two appendix sections, a multilingual cross-reference in Section 4.1, an abstract code-access sentence, and a corresponding-author designation. Subsequent appendices are relabeled; the existing narrative receives no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds multilingual and MMLU-category tables and expands the evaluation-prompt display. Figure 5 and several existing appendix tables are repositioned, with associated text reflow and renumbering. Original figures and existing table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 provides useful evidence for multilingual applicability and isolates filtering benefits across MMLU categories, while improving code-access information and prompt documentation. These gains are limited by the unspecified mIFEval metric and absent uncertainty reporting; the category accuracies also do not directly establish the proposed determinism mechanism. Overall, empirical support and documentation improve without changing the core method.
